title: Credential provisioning workflow and priority scoring for org admins
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers frequently request privileged admin access, SCIM provisioning, or SSO onboarding in ways that are time-consuming for support and potentially risky if mis-scoped. Current intake is ad-hoc: security must review each case, engineering builds custom mappings, and CS owners manually prioritize.

Goal: Define a deterministic credential provisioning workflow plus an automated priority-scoring heuristic that routes admin & access requests (RBAC changes, SSO/SAML enablement, SCIM mapping, org-level policy exemptions) through the right intake path: self-serve, expedited automation, solution engineering, or security-led review. Reduce time-to-complete for low-risk requests to <48h, surface high-risk requests to security within 4h, and cut manual engineering mapping work by 40% in H1 2026.

Scope: RBAC template provisioning, SSO/SAML enablement checklist, SCIM attribute mapping presets, priority scoring algorithm, intake UI/fields, webhook/automation triggers to create Engineering or SE flows, and docs/templated answers for support reps.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form fields standardized for all admin requests (requestor org, requested role, justification, affected routes/models, desired SSO provider, SCIM schema sample).
Priority score computed and visible in ticket (score components: org_size, contract_tier, security_profile, SLA_requirement, requested_scope).
Automated route: requests scoring below threshold create a self-serve task and trigger template provisioning (RBAC template + standard SCIM mapping).
Escalation route: high-score requests create a security review task and notify SE with required artifact checklist.
Engineering workload reduced via reusable SCIM mapping presets and a new RBAC template library (3 initial templates).
End-to-end SOC/Compliance checklist included for each expedited path and stored in audit logs.
milestones: M1: Draft intake schema and scoring rubric (2025-11-26)
M2: Prototype intake UI and RBAC template library (2025-12-10)
M3: Implement automated routing webhooks and SCIM presets (2025-12-22)
M4: Pilot with three enterprise customers and iterate (2026-01-10)
M5: Ship console rollout and document runbook (2026-01-30)
decisions: Use a numeric priority score (0-100) combining objective signals; thresholds drive routing rather than freeform triage.
Start with 3 RBAC templates (Org Admin, Billing Admin, Support Operator) and expand based on pilot feedback.
SCIM presets to cover common IdP schemas (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace) and provide a sample JSON mapping uploader for custom mappings.
Security retains final veto on any expedited automation; automated path logs an auditable record with snapshot of requested privileges.
implementation_notes: Backend: Add new intake endpoint /admin-intake that enriches tickets with computed priority_score and policy_flags.
Frontend: Intake modal on Console > Admins with dynamic help text and example SCIM payloads.
Automation: Use existing orchestration queue (ENG-4478) to spawn SE tasks, or trigger self-serve provisioning Lambda for low-risk templates.
Data: Instrument metrics: time_to_first_action, time_to_complete, % routed to self-serve, % security-reviewed, and post-provision incident rate.
review_comments: PM note (2025-11-13): Lean on existing RBAC role model in runtime-1.18 rather than introducing new role primitives.
Eng feedback (Samuel Ortiz, 2025-11-15): We can reuse the KV cache for storing template snapshots, but need a migration plan for old manual mappings.
Security feedback (Maya Chen, 2025-11-16): Add multi-factor verification step for any request that grants >= write access to model routes; include required justification fields.
Design feedback (Lina Gomez, 2025-11-18): Intake modal needs progressive disclosure for SCIM advanced options to avoid overwhelming small orgs.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-automation could grant excessive privileges to misclassified requests. Mitigation: conservative low-risk threshold and mandatory audit snapshot plus 24h manual review window for all automated grants.
Risk: SCIM mappings mis-map attributes leading to account collisions. Mitigation: provide a dry-run simulation and require customer confirmation before finalizing mappings.
Risk: High engineering churn supporting custom templates. Mitigation: limit initial launch to templates plus a paid 'custom mapping' professional services path.
rollback_plan: Disable automated provisioning webhook and mark affected tickets for manual review.
Revoke recent RBAC grants created by automation and notify affected org admins and SEs.
Open incident ticket and run postmortem; use retained audit logs to reconstruct provisioning decisions.
pilot_plan: Recruit 3 customers across Small, Mid, and Enterprise tiers for pilot; include one current customer with custom SCIM mapping history.
Run pilot for 4 weeks, collect qualitative feedback from SEs/CS, and measure ticket handling metrics.
Iterate RBAC template permissions, adjust priority thresholds, and add one additional SCIM preset based on usage.
notes: This ticket synthesizes repeated customer asks: fast SSO enablement, templated RBAC, and clearer routing for security-sensitive admin requests.
Aim to make the intake extensible so that Dedicated/Private customers can opt into stricter policies or an approval workflow backed by their own IdP.
